writeups.t: Easy as GDB — Scripted Character-by-Character Brute Force
writeups.d: The flag is validated one character at a time, so automate it: script GDB to brute-force the key space inside a single session.
writeups.b: A single challenge description line — "The flag has got to be checked somewhere..." — is almost the whole solution. The attached 32-bit ELF ( brute ) asks for a flag candidate, encodes it on the fly, then walks the encoded bytes against the stored encoded flag one position at a time, aborting at the first mismatch. That per-byte compare is an oracle you can mine directly: set a breakpoint on the compare instruction, count hits, and read AL / DL to decide each character. This is the challenge that GDB's Python scripting API was made for. 1 · First Run — Meet the Oracle The program is a key chec

writeups.t: Keygenme — MD5 Hex Spliced Into a License Key
writeups.d: The binary assembles the full 36-character key on the stack out of two MD5 digests — so the lazy solve is to break in and read it out.
writeups.b: "Can you get the flag?" — picoCTF 2022 is done teasing: most RE challenges ask you to break a check, this one asks you to produce the key that passes it. The catch is the binary already knows the full 36-character key: it assembles it on the stack out of a hardcoded prefix, two MD5 digests and a closing brace, right before comparing it against your input. So the laziest solve isn't writing a keygen at all — it's breaking inside the checker and string-searching the fully-built key from memory. 1 · First Run — It Wants a License Key gdb keygenme gef➤ r Starting program .../keygenme Enter your li

writeups.t: Binary Instrumentation 2 — Intercepting File Writes With Frida
writeups.d: picoCTF 2025 · 300 pts. Hook the file-write API with Frida and rewrite the payload before it ever touches disk.
writeups.b: picoCTF 2025, 300 points. A Windows binary that "was supposed to create a file and write the flag to it" — but when you run it, no file appears and no flag prints. The challenge's name is the hint: instrument the binary at runtime and fix what its WinAPI calls do as they happen. 1 · Run It — Nothing Happens The program is a GUI-free console bininst2.exe that exits immediately doing, apparently, nothing interesting. Strings inspection points to CreateFileA and WriteFile (KERNEL32). The bug is upstream, in the code that called them. 2 · Trace File APIs With Frida Frida's frida-trace auto-generat
